To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the aminopeni-cillin/inhibitor and older cephalos- porin combinations are still effective against most of the oral pathogens, but that cefetamet is more effective than the other cephalosporin derivatives.

cefetamet has a good in vitro activity against Enterobacter species, Klebsiella species, and Haemophilus species, but it is not active against the staphylococci and streptococcal species; the aminopenillin/beta-lactamase inhibitors are active against the strepococci and Enterobacteriacea but they are not active against the Haemophilus and Moraxella species.

the aminopeni-cillin/beta-lactamase inhibitors are highly active against the Streptococcus species, whereas cefadroxill and cefaclor were the most active compounds against the gram-positive coccet, and cefetamet is the most active compound among the cephalosporin class against the Enterobacteriaceac.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the evaluation of antimicrobial activity of a number of oral antibiotics in Italy, and the results are compared with those reported in the literature.

the evaluation of the susceptibility of clinical isolates to oral antibiotics, in an attempt to provide a useful tool to the clinician for the choice of the most suitable antibiotic for the treatment of the most common infections.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the susceptibility of oral isolates in Italy is similar to the one reported in the literature for the same species.

cefetamet should be considered a valuable oral agent in the treatment of urinary tract infections and respiratory tract infections, whereas the use of the aminopen-icillins and the older cephamycins should be limited to infections due to the streptococcaceae.
cefetamet and the beta-lactams plus beta-lactam inhibitor combinations are the best choices for the treatment of respiratory tract infections.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the new cephalosporin cefetamet is a good alternative to the older cephalosporsins for treatment of urinary tract infections and respiratory tract infections, and that the beta-lactanase inhibitor combination amoxicillin plus sulbacteram is the drug of choice against streptococcal infections.

cefetamet and amoxicillin/clavulanate are the best choices for the empirical therapy of infections caused by the Enterobacteriacea and Streptococcus pyogenes, whereas cefadroxyl and amoxicillin are the drugs of choice for the empirical treatment of infections caused by S. pneumoniae.
cefetamet is the most promising compound among the ones tested, whereas the aminopenillin/beta-lactamase inhibitors are the least promising ones.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there are still a number of compounds available for oral use which are active against the majority of bacterial strains.

the aminopeniclins and beta-lactam inhibitors are not as good as the cephalosporin compounds, especially the third generation ones, and the macrolide and the tetracycline compounds, for the treatment of infections caused by the Enterobacteriacea.
there are no major problems with resistance in Italy, but there are still some areas of concern.
